reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history, a midpoint wage balances margin and chance of winning against an unknown rival wage.
With equal revenue per labor, a positive wage earns profit only if it wins; 10 balances margin and chance of winning without history.
A tie at 10 earned 5; undercutting by 1 wins labor for profit 9, while raising risks losing it. Keep 10 to preserve the split pending more evidence.
Matching B’s last wage preserves half the labor and earns 5; with no evidence B will change, 10 is a reasonable repeat.
C matched 10 twice, splitting labor. Holding preserves the current outcome while learning whether C changes its wage.
B has matched 10 twice; matching preserves an equal split at a positive profit. With no evidence of a deviation, continue coordinating at 10.
C has matched 10 for three rounds. Holding preserves the tie and earns 5; undercutting gives at most a small gain if C stays at 10, while risking lower profit if C responds.
Matching B preserves the equal split at the observed wage, yielding 5 profit with no evidence of a deviation. One round remains after this, so avoid an untested undercut.
Matching C at 10 has yielded a reliable split and profit of 5. Raising risks lowering profit if matched; cutting sacrifices margin. With five rounds left, hold at 10 and reassess after observing C.
B has held at 10, so matching preserves half the labor and earns 5; undercutting would sacrifice margin for the whole unit.
C has matched 10 every round. Matching preserves a half share at 5 profit; undercutting gains the whole unit but earns less, while raising loses the labor.
B has held at 10 for five rounds, so matching preserves the known equal split and earns 5 this round.

C has matched 10 every round. Holding earns 5 if matched; undercutting slightly may win the unit but yields less profit, while raising risks losing it. With three rounds left, maintain the established match.
Matching the stable wage preserves half the labor and earns 5; undercutting yields less per unit, while raising risks losing all labor if B stays at 10.
C has matched 10 every round. Holding preserves the split and earns 5; undercutting gives up profit, while raising risks losing all labor.

B has held at 10 for seven rounds. Matching earns C 5; undercutting by one would earn 9 this round but risks disrupting the profitable pattern. With three rounds left, keep matching absent evidence B will move.
C has matched 10 for eight rounds. With one round after this, holding 10 preserves the split profit of 5 without risking a lower margin or losing labor.
B has consistently matched 10, giving each firm profit 5. With one round left, matching preserves that outcome; undercutting gives at most 9, while bidding above 10 risks a loss.

C has matched 10 in every round. In the final round, matching secures half the labor for profit 5; undercutting by 1 wins all labor but yields profit 9, while a higher wage earns zero. With no evidence C will change, 9 is the best exploitation of the likely 10 offer.
B has held at 10 for nine rounds. Matching secures half the labor for profit 5; undercutting yields only 1 more profit if B stays at 10, while risking a costly wage war.
